answers.core: To me the main use case of this would be looking at a target while rotating at a constant value, which would be useful for something like a turret or homing missile off the top of my head. I think these would share the use cases with `slerp`, with this being mostly preferential.
answers.workaround: The functions can be recreated (or copied from here) as static functions. But some implementations of it I saw can cause a division by zero near the end.
